1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.03.2023.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 16.03.2023 at about 2.15 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Devanahalli Traffic Police Station, near old Bus stand Devanahalli, M.V.C.No.2204/2023 3 SCCH - 7 Bengaluru Rural district, the Petitioner/ PW-1 drove the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-11-EE- 3954 from Vijayapura Cross and when he was taking U- turn at the right side near old Bus stand the accused drove the offending TATA Tempo vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AA-2801 from Old BB Road New Bus stand towards old Bus stand in a rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner/PW-1 sustained grievous on both bones of left leg.

Thereafter he has shifted to Manasa Hospital,
Devanahalli and thereafter for higher treatment he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and underwent surgery therein.
Thereafter, Petitioner has given the statement before the Police of Devanahalli Traffic police station while taking treatment in the New Manasa Hospital.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that,
Petitioner sustained grievous injury due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed the said Accused/ driver to be M.V.C.No.2204/2023 15 SCCH - 7 innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to no fault of the accused, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

20. On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, MVA Report, Wound Certificate, Charge Sheet, Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to the Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act,
and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged M.V.C.No.2204/2023 16 SCCH - 7 by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle in which the rider of the unoffending vehicle was taking U-turn at the spot road, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR,
Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P3/Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4/Spot sketch, Ex.P5/MVA Report, Ex.P-6/Wound Certificate, Ex.P-7/Charge Sheet, Ex.P.8/Police Intimation, Ex.P.9/ Discharge Summary,
Ex.P10/Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act and Ex.P11/reply to Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot shown in the Ex.P-4/Spot Sketch.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.

It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P- 5/MVA report,
Ex.P6/Wound Certificate and Ex.P- 10/Discharge Summary would be caused by a road traffic accident.

At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and M.V.C.No.2204/2023 17 SCCH - 7 fault of the accused/driver.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 338 of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.20,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

23. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 34 years and he was doing loading and unloading work at Bengaluru International Airport, Devanahalli and earning an income of Rs.20,000/- p.m.
The petitioner relied on the Ex.P.15/Adhar Card of the Petitioner and wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 16.10.1988 and this accident was took place on 16.03.2023.
Hence it is clear that on the strength of the Ex.P-15/Adhar Card as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 35 years.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 35 years.
24. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the alleged road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.

In the instance case the petitioner M.V.C.No.2204/2023 19 SCCH - 7 claimed that he was doing loading and unloading work at Bengaluru International Airport, Devanahalli and earning an income of Rs.20,000/- p.m.
But he has not produced any documents to prove the income of the Petitioner.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the Petitioner taken at Rs.15,250/-.

Somashekar, Orthopedics Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained type I open fracture both bones left leg and he undergone wound debridement, ORIF with plating for fibula and CRIF with IMIL nailing of tibia under CSEA on 21.03.2023.

26. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as loader and unloader, while doing loading and unloading work the petitioner has to stand and sit for long time, he has to bend, put weight on both hands and legs, he has to use hands and legs and he has to sit down, climbing upstairs and walk while doing the work.
But due to the injuries sustained in this accident the petitioner has not in position to do the said work as past.
The doctor has assessed the total disability of left lower limb at 41% and whole body disability is 20%.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 20% to the whole body.
27. With regard to the quantum, the age of the petitioner is considered as 35 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,250/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 16 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 20%.

On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is M.V.C.No.2204/2023 22 SCCH - 7 calculated as (Rs.15,250/- X 12 X 16 X 20/100) = Rs.5,85,600/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.5,85,600/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the alleged accident.

28. In the alleged accident the petitioner has sustained type I open fracture both bones left leg and he undergone wound debridement, ORIF with plating for fibula and CRIF with IMIL nailing of tibia under CSEA which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering,

opennyai_summary.facts:
1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.03.2023.
2.
Accordingly,
a case was registered in their Crime No.63/2023 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279 and 338 of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he became permanently disabled and he is unable to do his work normally as he was doing prior to the occurrence of the alleged accident.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Tempo bearing registration No.KA-19-AA-2801 and Respondent No.1 is the RC owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.
Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and further the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. Act., and the driver of the offending car did not possess the valid and effective driving licence as on the date of occurrence of the accident and violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:
:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of offending Tempo bearing registration No.KA-19- AA-2801 and as a result, he has sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the petitioner proves that age and earnings of the petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
(4) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Respondent No.2/Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the injured Petitioner and the said Petitioner suddenly taken U-turn at the spot with taking note of the approaching the offending vehicle.
There is every possibility of dashing against the offending vehicle without the driver becoming aware of it.
The driver of the offending vehicle cannot save accident, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent and therefore the entire negligence ought to have been held against the rider of the unoffending Motor Cycle.
Hence the rider of the unoffending has equally contributed to the accident.
Further it is alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident and violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed the said Accused/ driver to be M.V.C.No.2204/2023 15 SCCH - 7 innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to no fault of the accused, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Petitioner sustained grievous injury due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged M.V.C.No.2204/2023 16 SCCH - 7 by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle in which the rider of the unoffending vehicle was taking U-turn at the spot road, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P- 5/MVA report,
Ex.P6/Wound Certificate and Ex.P- 10/Discharge Summary would be caused by a road traffic accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and M.V.C.No.2204/2023 17 SCCH - 7 fault of the accused/driver.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 338 of IPC.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
opennyai_summary.decision:
On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is M.V.C.No.2204/2023 22 SCCH - 7 calculated as (Rs.15,250/- X 12 X 16 X 20/100) = Rs.5,85,600/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.5,85,600/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the alleged accident.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.30,000/- (Rs.2,000/- per day X 15) under head of special diet and conveyance.
30. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
